title: Canary Oncall Shifts and Telemetry Mapping — sandbox
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is a sandbox working doc to prototype a lightweight oncall pattern for canary/A-B releases that explicitly ties people shifts to telemetry mappings and escalation behaviors. Goal: reduce reaction time for emergent quality/latency/cost regressions during progressive exposures while keeping human workload bounded.

Context / motivations:
- We have many rollout runbooks and telemetry dashboards, but ownership and shift handoffs are informal and cause delay at 2–4am windows.
- LLM rollouts can show non-obvious behavioral regressions (safety, hallucination) that need human review, and engineering SLOs (latency/cost) that need immediate mitigation triggers.
- Existing docs focus on traffic-slicing and fallback; this doc focuses on the human-operational layer: who is watching, what exact signals they watch, and how they escalate.

Key principles:
1) Minimal watch team: 1 steward + 1 observer during working hours; nights/weekends shrink to a single responder for critical rollouts only.
2) Signal triage map: every oncall shift gets a one-pager mapping of "top 6" signals and quick triage actions (see table below).
3) Fast safe-fallback: default posture is automated partial rollback and traffic-slice quarantine for class-B regressions; human approval required for full rollback.
4) Psychological safety: responders must be able to declare a "soft pause" (stop exposure, preserve data, call a postmortem) without manager approval.

Proposed shift roles and responsibilities:
- Steward (primary): owns the canary during the shift window. Responsible for triage, executing curated mitigation recipes, and running the post-exposure notes.
- Observer (secondary): watches broader system health, triages alerts that are not obviously canary-related, acts as scribe during incidents.
- Responder (emergency-only): senior oncall from eng-sre or serving-runtime to apply code-level hotfixes or capacity adjustments.
- Communications steward (rotated across PM/Product Ops): owns stakeholder comms and decision logs when exposure crosses defined thresholds.

Suggested rota (example):
- Weekdays 09:00–18:00 PST: Steward (product rollout owner), Observer (oncall engineer); 1-hour overlap at shift handover.
- Weekdays 18:00–23:00 PST: Steward (reduced scope — only high-risk releases), Observer (SRE oncall).
- Nights/weekends: Oncall responder on rotation but only paged for SEV-level signals; non-urgent items create a ticket and wake the weekday steward.
- Canary windows shorter than 2 hours avoid nighttime paging.

Telemetry mapping (top signals and quick actions):
- Signal A: Median P95 latency for inference (per-model). Alert if P95 > baseline * 1.5 for 10min. Quick action: pause new inference routing to canary model variant; switch to warm fallback model.
- Signal B: Token-cost per request (avg tokens * cost-per-token). Alert if cost spike > 2x baseline OR sustained for 30min. Quick action: throttle rate-limited routes, enable model quantization config or route to cheaper variant.
- Signal C: Safety regression proxy (human-review rate for flagged outputs). Alert if user-reported rate > 0.5% and doubling week-over-week. Quick action: reduce exposure, enable human-review cohort, tag sample set for QA.
- Signal D: Response correctness failure rate (reranker accuracy drop / golden prompts). Alert if drop >5% in key cohort. Quick action: rollback to previous model version for affected slice and trigger model evaluation job.
- Signal E: Error budget burn (5xxs per minute). Alert if error rate crosses 1.0% sustained for 5min. Quick action: scale up dedicated pool, enable circuit-breaker that diverts to hosted API.
- Signal F: Observability instrumentation gaps (missing KV cache metrics, invalid traces). Alert if telemetry missing for >2min. Quick action: triage with SRE; preserve traffic sample and mark observations as unreliable until restored.

Handoff checklist (to be completed in shift notes):
- Current active canaries and slices with start times and % exposure.
- Two-sentence summary of known risks and mitigations in place.
- Links to dashboards (keep 3 concise links).
- Outstanding followups requiring next shift.
- Snapshot commit / model version pinned for the runway.

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Level 1 (on-shift steward): Triage + apply canned mitigation (pause/route, scale, throttle).
- Level 2 (oncall responder): If mitigation not effective in 10–15 minutes, escalate; responder runs capacity or code-level fix.
- Level 3 (pager + exec comms): If user-visible safety/regulatory issue, immediately page product security lead and set communication channel (Slack #rollout-incidents), prepare incident brief.

Templates (copyable):
- Slack paging message: "Paging @responder — Canary [model:eval-2026-01] at 14:32 PST: P95 latency 1.9s (+80%); rolling pause requested. Steward: @Aisha. Context: link to dashboard. Action taken: paused slice 42%. Next: scale pool + run regression check.
- Short decision log line: "2026-03-09 14:35 PST — Pause slice 42% on model eval-2026-01 due to P95 surge. Steward: Aisha. Escalated to SRE: Ethan.

Post-canary lightweight report (to be filled within 24 hours):
- Start/end times and exposure curve.
- Top signals triggered and mitigation timeline.
- Customer-facing impact (if any) and number of complaints or failures.
- Lessons learned + recommended config changes for next run.

Known gaps and open questions (short):
- How to route synthetic canary traffic for safety signals without influencing user metrics? (Marco to prototype)
- Do we need a separate human-review cohort for privacy-sensitive customers? (legal/security input needed)
- Nighttime coverage cost vs risk tradeoff: what % of canaries should be blocked from reaching nights? (product ops)

Action items / next steps:
- Marco: prototype a condensed 3-link "steward page" per canary that loads in <2s (prototype due 2026-03-21).
- Sana: draft minimal pager templates and Slack playbooks, prioritize clarity for non-engineering stakeholders (due 2026-03-18).
- Ethan: write a short runbook snippet for the responder path that includes exact k8s commands and rollback steps (due 2026-03-17).
- Priya: collect legal/security guidance on human-review cohorts for PHI/protected customers (sync by 2026-03-24).

Quick notes / heuristics for stewards:
- If two distinct top signals fire within a 15-minute window, default to quarantine + snapshot, then escalate.
- Preserve sample traces and do not overwrite logs for the next 24 hours after any mitigation.
- Use the minimal change necessary to reduce customer impact (reduce exposure % vs full rollback).

References and bookmarks (internal):
- Canary signal catalog — Confluence (linked above).
- Release traffic slicing playbook (see shared drive folder).
- Pager duty escalation policy for product rollouts.

This doc is intentionally prescriptive but experimental. Aim: ship a first lightweight rotation for Q2 pilot and iterate based on actual oncall load and false-positive rate.

Unresolved: perfecting the safety regression proxy and mapping it to automated gating is the highest-value follow-up.

---
Notes to self: keep this file as the single source for the human-ops experiment. Move stable templates into the rollout-runbook repo after pilot.
